theme: p75NTR neurotrophin signalling: survival versus death
story: The centre is NGF and proNGF signalling through the p75 neurotrophin receptor, with p75NTR recruiting adaptor complexes, undergoing regulated proteolysis and sending death signals via NRAGE-JNK, NRIF, NADE and ceramide, or survival signals via NF-kB. TRKA activation by NGF, PLC-gamma1, STAT3 and retrograde signalling are the pro-survival/trophic arm, while NGF processing and neurotrophin production supply the ligands and dependence-receptor pathways (NTRK3, caspase activation without ligand) add the ligand-withdrawal death logic. Together the cluster describes how neurotrophins decide whether neurons and glia live or die.

theme: Cell cycle control: G1/S and G2/M checkpoints
story: The core is the cell-cycle engine: RB1-E2F/DREAM control of G1/S transcription, cyclin D/E-CDK activity and its degradation, and cyclin A/B-CDK1 events with Polo-like kinase and MASTL driving G2/M. TP53 regulation (phosphorylation, degradation, COP1) and Chk1/Chk2-Cdc25A arms provide checkpoint brakes, while CDK inhibitor degradation, CDK4/6 drug inhibition, RB1 mutant defects and oncogene-induced senescence show how the machinery fails or is targeted in cancer. The cluster as a whole represents the regulated progression of the mitotic cell cycle and its checkpoints.

theme: Renal renin-angiotensin control of blood pressure and volume
story: The centre is the renin-angiotensin system: angiotensinogen processing to angiotensins, angiotensin receptor signalling and regulation of angiotensin levels acting on the kidney to control blood volume. Renal processes (glomerular filtration, sodium excretion, urine volume, albumin absorption) are the effectors, while vasopressin, nervous control, and cGMP/natriuretic guanylyl cyclase signalling plus bradykinin/neuropeptide catabolism (ACE-type peptidase activity) act as modulating inputs. Together they describe systemic arterial pressure and fluid homeostasis via kidney and vasoactive peptides.

theme: Hindbrain development and motor behaviour
story: The core is development of the brainstem, pons, hindbrain and cerebellar Purkinje layer, together with motor-neuron survival and substantia nigra development. These structures underlie the behavioural members: locomotion, walking, motor learning, proprioception, righting reflex, suckling and neural control of breathing. A neural RNA-binding module (ELAVL3, CPEB3, YBX1) is a looser companion, so the cluster as a whole links hindbrain/motor circuit formation to coordinated movement and basic reflex behaviours.

theme: Glycogen, glycolysis, gluconeogenesis and fructose metabolism
story: The centre is hepatic and muscle glucose handling: glycogen synthesis and breakdown, glycolysis, gluconeogenesis and fructose-2,6-bisphosphate regulation, with fructose catabolism and glycerol/alditol metabolism feeding into the same hexose-phosphate pool. Many members are inborn errors of these steps (glycogen storage diseases, Lafora disease, hereditary fructose intolerance, essential fructosuria, PGM1-CDG, GCK-MODY, HK deficiency, G6PC3 neutropenia) that map defects onto the pathway. Peripheral items like alanine, lactate, phosphocreatine and oxygen transport reflect energy metabolism links; overall the cluster is central carbohydrate storage and fuel metabolism.

theme: TLR2/TLR4 bacterial lipid sensing
story: The core is detection of bacterial cell-wall lipids, LPS via LBP-CD14 transfer to TLR4 and lipoteichoic acid/diacyl lipopeptides via TLR2, with positive and negative regulation of these receptors. MyD88 and IRAK4 deficiencies (affecting TLR2/4 and TLR5) represent the shared downstream adaptor axis and its immunodeficiency diseases, and leukocyte chemotaxis is the inflammatory outcome. The cluster as a whole is innate recognition of bacterial products through TLR-MyD88 signalling.

theme: Protein lysine and arginine methylation, including histones
story: The centre is protein methylation: mono-, di- and trimethylation of lysine and arginine methylation, applied to histones by arginine methyltransferases and reversed by histone demethylases. Methylation of non-histone substrates such as TP53, RUNX1 co-factors and the CHD1/CHD2 chromatin remodellers that read methyl marks complete the picture. Together the cluster describes methylation as a regulatory modification of chromatin and transcription factors.

theme: Proteasome and MHC class I antigen presentation
story: The core is the proteasome, its assembly and ubiquitin-independent degradation, generating peptides for MHC class I loading. Endogenous presentation and cross-presentation of exogenous antigens via ER-phagosome and endosomal/vacuolar routes, cytosol-to-ER transport and peptide loading/assembly of class I complexes form the presentation arm, with CD8 T cell homeostasis as the immunological outcome. The cluster represents how cells process proteins into class I peptides for CD8 T cell surveillance.

theme: Actin filament dynamics and cytoskeletal remodelling
story: The core is regulation of actin filament architecture: severing, depolymerisation, barbed-end capping, crosslinking, network formation and inhibition of Arp2/3 nucleation. RHOF GTPase and EPHB forward signalling are upstream inputs that reshape actin, while cell polarity/shape and caspase cleavage of cytoskeletal proteins are its cellular outcomes. Together they describe how the actin cytoskeleton is assembled, remodelled and dismantled.

theme: Cardiac conduction system and pacemaker action potentials
story: The centre is regulation of cardiac conduction and heart rate, from SA node depolarisation (with HCN pacemaker channels) through the bundle of His and Purkinje fibres to ventricular myocytes. Gap junction assembly and electrical coupling between conducting cells are the mechanism carrying the impulse, and action potential regulation links it to contraction. The cluster as a whole describes generation and propagation of the heartbeat's electrical signal.

theme: Skeletal development: bone, cartilage, joints and tendon
story: The core is bone formation, including osteoblast development, intramembranous (direct) ossification, trabecular bone formation and regulation of bone development. Cartilage morphogenesis, joint and cranial suture morphogenesis and tendon development complete the skeletal and connective structures that articulate with bone. Together they describe building the skeleton and its joints.

theme: tRNA and rRNA processing and modification, especially mitochondrial
story: The centre is tRNA maturation, 5' leader removal, 3'-end processing, intron splicing, and chemical modifications such as methylation, pseudouridylation and wybutosine, in both nucleus and mitochondrion. rRNA modification (2'-O-methylation via box C/D snoRNPs, base methylation, pseudouridylation) and mitochondrial ribosomal subunit assembly, mRNA modification and translation regulation complete the translation-apparatus side. The cluster as a whole is the processing and modification of non-coding RNAs that build a functional translation system, with a strong mitochondrial component.

theme: Synaptic calcium-CaMK-CREB signalling in memory
story: The core is activity-dependent signalling from postsynaptic NMDA receptor calcium influx to the nucleus via CaMKII/CaMKK/CaMKIV phosphorylating CREB and inducing NPAS4. AMPK activation downstream of NMDARs and CAMKK-AMPK regulation are a parallel branch of the same kinase cascade. The outcome is long-term potentiation and short- and long-term memory, so the cluster describes synapse-to-nucleus signalling underlying learning.

theme: TLR-driven IKK/TAK1 activation of NF-kB
story: The centre is the TLR signalling hub that activates NF-kB: TRAF6- and IRAK1/2-mediated activation of TAK1 and IKK recruitment downstream of MyD88-dependent TLR7/8/9 and TRIF/TICAM1-RIP1-dependent TLR4/TLR3 signalling. TRAF6-mediated IRF7 activation provides the interferon branch, while SUMOylation of immune proteins and NF-kB/TNF regulation tune the response. Together it describes how innate receptors converge on kinase complexes to activate inflammatory transcription.

theme: Renal transport of organic anions and metabolites
story: The core is membrane transport of small organic anions, succinate, alpha-ketoglutarate, tricarboxylates, pyruvate and carnitine, notably by sodium-coupled SLC13 and organic cation/anion SLC22 transporters. Proximal tubule development and carnitine deficiency (SLC22A5) point to the kidney as the main site, while GLUT1 deficiency is a looser transport-disease companion. The cluster as a whole describes carrier-mediated uptake of metabolic intermediates, especially in renal tubules.

theme: Hexose, pentose phosphate and sugar interconversion metabolism
story: The centre is central sugar metabolism linking glycolysis and gluconeogenesis to the non-oxidative pentose phosphate pathway, xylulose-5-phosphate and PRPP synthesis, the glucuronate-xylulose pathway, and galactose (Leloir) and fructose catabolism. Many members are inborn errors (galactosaemias GALT/GALK1/GALE/GALM, TALDO1 and RPIA deficiency, pentosuria, fructosuria, fructose intolerance, HK deficiency) mapping defects onto these routes, while glycerol, inositol and alditol metabolism are side branches. The cluster as a whole is the network that interconverts dietary sugars into glycolytic and nucleotide-precursor intermediates.

theme: Axon guidance by netrin, SLIT-ROBO and ephrin
story: The centre is axon guidance via the major cue-receptor systems: netrin-DCC attraction and repulsion, SLIT-ROBO repulsion and ephrin-EPH repulsion with growth cone collapse. These converge on Rho-family GTPases (RAC1/RAC3 activation, CDC42/RAC1 inactivation, RHOA via SLIT2-ROBO1, ABL) that remodel the growth cone cytoskeleton. Outcomes include axon extension, chemorepulsion and fasciculation, so the cluster describes how axons are steered to their targets.

theme: Systemic blood pressure regulation by vasoactive and renal systems
story: The centre is regulation of systemic arterial blood pressure, positive and negative, through the renin-angiotensin system (angiotensin generation, levels and receptor signalling) acting on renal sodium excretion, urine volume and blood volume. Vasoconstriction control by endothelin, vasopressin and the nervous system, and vasodilatory nitric oxide/cGMP-guanylyl cyclase signalling, act as opposing vascular arms, with lung pressure as an extension. Together they describe the integrated hormonal, neural and renal control of blood pressure.

theme: DNA replication licensing and initiation under E2F control
story: The core is origin licensing and firing: ORC-CDC6 association, pre-replicative complex activation, Orc1 removal and initiation of cell-cycle DNA replication. E2F transcription networks provide the upstream transcriptional control of these replication genes and also inhibit re-licensing, while the replication checkpoint and ATR activation by replication stress are the safeguards. The cluster as a whole describes how S-phase DNA replication is licensed, initiated and protected.

theme: Adherens junctions and epithelial cell-cell adhesion
story: The centre is assembly, maintenance and protein localisation of adherens junctions, mediating calcium-dependent cadherin cell-cell adhesion. Epithelial cell-cell adhesion and apical junction gene sets, with membrane/cell-junction component sets, describe the same structures from a different angle. Together they represent the junctional complexes that hold epithelial sheets together.

theme: Phosphate homeostasis and mineralisation
story: The core is regulation of phosphate ion transport and intracellular phosphate homeostasis, involving sodium-dependent phosphate transporters (SLC34A1, SLC20A2) and responses to phosphate. Endocrine control comes from PTH and FGF23-type signalling through FGFR1c-Klotho and FGFR-MAPK, while bone mineralisation and ectopic-calcification diseases (PXE from ABCC6, basal ganglia calcification) are the tissue outcomes. The cluster describes how phosphate levels are sensed, transported and hormonally controlled to govern mineralisation.

theme: Regulation of mitochondrial respiration and oxidative stress
story: The centre is regulation of oxidative phosphorylation: electron transport from NADH to ubiquinone, ATP synthesis-coupled transport, and positive and negative control of cellular respiration and ATP production. ROS generation and oxidative stress responses, hypoxia responses and nucleotide biosynthesis reflect the redox and energy consequences, while drug/antibiotic responses and developmental apoptosis are looser associated outcomes. Together it represents control of mitochondrial energy production and its redox side-effects.

theme: Regulation of thymocyte and B lymphocyte development
story: The core is regulation of T cell development in the thymus: immature T cell proliferation (both directions), thymocyte survival and T cell differentiation. Regulation of pro-B cell and B cell differentiation and hematopoietic progenitor differentiation place this within broader lymphopoiesis. Together the cluster describes control of early lymphocyte lineage development from progenitors.

theme: Synapse assembly and regulation of synaptic transmission
story: The centre is synapse formation, positive and negative regulation of synapse assembly, presynapse and terminal bouton organisation, and protein localisation to synapses. Inhibitory synapse assembly via gephyrin and GABA receptor clustering forms one arm, while regulation of excitatory and inhibitory postsynaptic potentials and glutamatergic transmission form the functional readout. Together the cluster describes building synapses and setting their excitatory-inhibitory transmission strength.

theme: Cytosolic nucleic acid sensing and type I interferon
story: The core is RIG-I/MDA5 (DDX58/IFIH1) and DEx/H-box helicase sensing of viral RNA, with cytosolic DNA sensing and ZBP1-RIP signalling as parallel sensors. These converge on IRF3-mediated type I interferon and interferon-alpha induction, with NF-kB, IP-10 production and dendritic cell activation as downstream outputs, and negative regulators tuning the system. Together the cluster describes the cell-intrinsic antiviral innate response.

theme: ERK MAPK signalling, feedback and IL-6/AP-1 output
story: The centre is ERK1/ERK2 activation and its negative feedback, inactivation and suppression, including signalling by MAPK mutants. AP-1 transcription factor activation is the main nuclear output, while IL-6-JAK-STAT3 signalling and autocrine signalling are coupled cytokine inputs that also engage MAPK. Together it describes the ERK-centred signalling loop that links cytokine/growth stimuli to AP-1 gene expression, with its brakes.

theme: mRNA 3'-end processing and histone mRNA maturation
story: The core is cleavage and polyadenylation of pre-mRNA 3' ends, coupled to RNA polymerase II transcription termination and processing of intronless transcripts. Replication-dependent histone mRNAs, which use stem-loop binding (SLBP) cleavage instead of polyadenylation, and their degradation form the specialised branch. Together it describes how mRNA 3' ends are formed and how this ends transcription.

theme: Development of mammary, prostate, pancreas and reproductive glands
story: The centre is glandular epithelial morphogenesis and differentiation, especially the mammary gland (branching, alveolar development, stem/luminal/myoepithelial lineages, lactation, thelarche) and prostate (budding, branching, acinar morphogenesis). Pancreatic progenitor and endocrine lineage specification, adrenal and neuroendocrine differentiation, and reproductive tract development (uterus, oviduct, vagina, genitalia) extend the same programme of hormone-responsive epithelial organ formation. The cluster as a whole is the development of glandular and reproductive epithelial organs.

theme: Epithelial-mesenchymal signalling in branching organ development
story: The core is reciprocal epithelial-mesenchymal signalling that drives branching morphogenesis, as in lung bud elongation, salivary gland branching, terminal-unit subdivision and lacrimal and mammary gland formation. Mesenchymal proliferation control supplies the stromal partner, while pancreatic, bile duct, kidney and hepatocyte nuclear factor-related items extend this to endodermal ductal organs and limb bud formation applies the same logic. Together it describes how epithelia and mesenchyme interact to build branched organs.

theme: Lipoprotein uptake and macrophage foam cell formation
story: The centre is lipoprotein particle signalling and transport that promotes cholesterol import and storage. In macrophages this drives foam cell differentiation, the cellular event of atherosclerosis, with pinocytosis regulation reflecting the uptake route. Together the cluster describes cholesterol loading of cells from lipoproteins.

theme: Axon guidance by netrin, SLIT-ROBO and ephrin
story: The core is axon guidance by netrin-DCC, SLIT-ROBO (including commissural pathfinding and regulation of SLIT/ROBO expression) and ephrin-EPH signalling, with anterior-posterior guidance and growth cone collapse. These cues act through Rho GTPases (RAC1/RAC3, CDC42, RHOA, ABL) on the cytoskeleton to promote or inhibit axon extension and repulsion, with fasciculation as an outcome. The cluster describes the molecular steering of axons during wiring of the nervous system.

theme: Xenobiotic and drug metabolism
story: The centre is phase I and II biotransformation of foreign compounds: cytochrome P450 reactions (CYP1A2, CYP2E1, oxidative demethylation), sulfonation, acetylation and methylation, exemplified by paracetamol ADME. Aryl hydrocarbon receptor signalling is the inducing sensor, and the many substrate classes (phenylpropanoids, polyketides, monoterpenoids, alkaloids, aromatic hydrocarbons, steroids) show the breadth of chemicals handled. Together the cluster describes detoxification and clearance of xenobiotics.

theme: Golgi-endosome-lysosome trafficking and retrograde transport
story: The core is vesicular traffic between the trans-Golgi network, endosomes and lysosomes: Golgi-associated and lysosomal vesicle biogenesis, Golgi-to-endosome/lysosome transport and protein targeting to lysosomes. Retrograde transport from early and late endosomes back to the Golgi and Golgi-to-ER retrieval, with Golgi retention and membrane docking/fusion, recycles the sorting machinery. Together it describes the post-Golgi sorting system that supports secretion and lysosome delivery.

theme: RAS-MAPK activation downstream of receptor adaptors
story: The centre is RAS activation by SOS via SHC adaptors, here downstream of IGF1R, and positive regulation of Ras signalling. MAP2K and RSK activation are the downstream kinase cascade, with oncogenic RAS and MAP2K mutants as disease forms and RIT/RIN-p38 a parallel small-GTPase branch. Together it describes growth factor receptor coupling to RAS and the MAPK cascade.

theme: Muscle growth and cardiac hypertrophic adaptation
story: The core is regulation of muscle cell size and growth, positive and negative, including cardiac muscle adaptation (hypertrophy) and cardiomyocyte growth. Skeletal muscle tissue growth, response to muscle activity and sarcomere organisation describe the same adaptive growth in skeletal muscle. Together the cluster represents how striated muscle grows in response to load.

theme: RAF-MEK-ERK signalling, oncogenic mutants and negative feedback
story: The centre is the RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK cascade: RAF activation, MAP2K and MAPK activation and RSK activation. Many members are oncogenic or RASopathy variants (BRAF high/moderate/kinase-dead mutants with paradoxical activation, RAF1 mutants and fusions, RAS mutants, MAP2K/MAPK mutants, NF1 loss, MRAS-SHOC2), while ERK inactivation, dephosphorylation and negative feedback provide the brakes. Together it describes MAPK pathway activation and its dysregulation in cancer and developmental disorders.

theme: Glutamate and aspartate transport and homeostasis
story: The core is excitatory amino acid transport: glutamate reuptake and L/D-aspartate import by SLC1-family transporters, and intracellular glutamate homeostasis. Astrocytic glutamate-glutamine cycling, glutamine import and serine transport and metabolism link this to neurotransmitter recycling, while transporter diseases (SLC1A1 schizophrenia/aminoaciduria, SLC1A3 episodic ataxia, SLC17A8 deafness) show its clinical importance. Together it describes how glutamate is cleared and recycled, especially at synapses.

theme: Selective autophagy and autophagosome regulation
story: The centre is autophagosome biogenesis and maturation, phagophore protein recruitment, substrate localisation and positive/negative regulation of assembly. Selective autophagy types (mitophagy, pexophagy, reticulophagy, nucleophagy) are the main specialised branches, with nutrient and oxygen-glucose deprivation as triggers. Protein delipidation (ATG8 deconjugation), depalmitoylation and UFMylation are modification steps tied to autophagy and ER-phagy, so the cluster as a whole describes autophagy and its cargo selection.

theme: Neuropeptide control of stress, arousal and social behaviour
story: The core is behavioural responses to stress, corticotropin-releasing hormone and corticosterone responses, immobilisation stress, the general adaptation syndrome and fear. Orexin and related neuropeptides regulate wakefulness and arousal, linking to the motivated and social behaviours (mating, parental, aggression, drinking, ethanol responses). Together the cluster describes hypothalamic neuropeptide and stress-hormone control of innate behaviour.

theme: Metal ion, gas and surfactant transport and homeostasis
story: The largest part is trace-metal homeostasis: iron (transferrin cycle, ferroportin, DMT1, heme scavenging and transport), zinc (SLC39/SLC30 families), copper, manganese, cadmium and metallothionein detoxification, with their deficiency and overload diseases. Erythrocyte gas exchange (O2/CO2, Rhesus ammonium transport, nitric oxide) and pulmonary surfactant metabolism and its SMDP diseases are distinct companion themes. The cluster as a whole is a broad grouping of membrane transport of metals, gases and related solutes rather than one tight pathway.

theme: FGF receptor signalling and activating FGFR mutants
story: The centre is FGFR1-4 ligand binding (including FGFR3b/3c isoforms and betaKlotho-dependent endocrine FGFs) and receptor activation. FRS2 and SHC adaptor cascades to RAS-MAPK and PLC-gamma signalling are the downstream arms, and activating point mutants of FGFR1-4 represent the disease forms seen in skeletal dysplasia and cancer. Together it describes FGF receptor signal transduction.

theme: Lipid modification and secretion of Wnt and Hedgehog ligands
story: The core is biogenesis and secretion of lipid-modified morphogens: PORCN palmitoleoylation of Wnt (with LGK974 inhibition) and Wnt secretion, and Hedgehog autoprocessing and HHAT palmitoylation with release from secreting cells and degradation of mutants by ERAD. Non-canonical Wnt/calcium signalling and WNT5A-dependent receptor internalisation are the downstream receiving side. Together the cluster describes how Wnt and Hh ligands are processed, lipidated and released to signal.

theme: Steroid hormone receptor signalling: estrogen, androgen, progesterone
story: The centre is estrogen receptor signalling, nuclear gene expression, membrane ESR and GPER1 signalling, and early and late estrogen responses. Androgen receptor signalling in prostate epithelium (KLK2/KLK3, PKN1, luminal secretory identity) and progesterone receptor signalling are parallel nuclear receptor arms, with HSP90 chaperoning, RUNX1 and TFAP2 as shared regulators. Together it describes sex steroid hormone action through nuclear receptors.

theme: Fibroblast activation, ECM deposition and fibrosis
story: The core is fibroblast behaviour in wound healing and fibrosis: connective tissue replacement, ECM assembly, collagen metabolism, myofibroblast and cardiac fibroblast differentiation, and fibroblast survival. TGF-beta response regulation is the main upstream driver, while miRNA transcription and processing act as post-transcriptional regulators of this fibrotic programme. Together it describes the control of tissue repair and scar formation.

theme: Catecholamine transport and dopamine synthesis
story: The centre is synaptic uptake and transport of catecholamines, dopamine and norepinephrine via monoamine transporters. Dopamine biosynthesis and regulation of catecholamine metabolism complete the life cycle of these transmitters. Together it describes monoamine neurotransmitter production and reuptake.

theme: Lysosomal fusion with autophagosomes, endosomes and phagosomes
story: The core is membrane fusion with lysosomes: autophagosome-lysosome, multivesicular body-lysosome, and phagosome-lysosome fusion, plus late endosome to lysosome transport. Endosomal and vacuole fusion supply the general fusion machinery, and SARS-CoV-2 modulation of autophagy shows how viruses target this step. Together it describes delivery of cargo to lysosomes for degradation.

theme: p53-mediated DNA damage checkpoint and cell cycle arrest
story: The centre is the DNA damage response through TP53: its phosphorylation and degradation (COP1), and its transcription of G1 and G2 arrest and DNA repair genes, triggered by gamma and X-ray radiation. G2 checkpoint signalling, Cdc25A degradation, CDK inhibition, GTSE1 and MASTL describe checkpoint enforcement and recovery, with replicative senescence as an outcome. PI3K-AKT-mTOR and a transcriptional-elongation gene module are looser companions; overall the cluster is genotoxic stress halting the cell cycle.

theme: Cellular cholesterol uptake, storage and efflux balance
story: The core is the balance of cellular cholesterol: import from lipoproteins and storage versus efflux and reverse cholesterol transport, with HDL clearance. LXR (NR1H3/NR1H2) transcriptional control of efflux genes is the regulatory hub. In macrophages this balance determines foam cell formation, so the cluster describes cholesterol homeostasis relevant to atherosclerosis.

theme: Unfolded protein response and integrated stress response
story: The centre is ER stress signalling: IRE1-XBP1 chaperone induction, PERK and ATF4 gene activation and the unfolded protein response, with stress-induced apoptosis including of pancreatic beta cells. The integrated stress response kinases HRI (heme deficiency, mitochondrial stress) and GCN2 (amino acid deficiency) converge with PERK on eIF2-mediated translational control, and the mitochondrial UPR is a parallel organelle arm. Together the cluster describes cellular proteostasis stress responses that reprogram translation and decide survival or death.

theme: FGFR and receptor tyrosine kinase downstream cascades
story: The core is FGFR1-4 ligand binding (FGFR3b/3c, betaKlotho) and activation. The downstream arms are SHC and FRS2-mediated RAS signalling, PI3K cascades and phospholipase C-gamma cascades with phosphatidylinositol signalling, with ERBB2 PLCG1 events as a related RTK example and FGFR3 activating mutants as disease forms. Together it describes FGF receptor signal transduction into its three main effector routes.
